questions.q: Why build and test a CRM Analytics app in a sandbox first?
options: Sandboxes have unlimited datasets
Change sets only work from production
So experiments are not visible to production users until the work is tested and promoted
Sandboxes make dashboards load faster for viewers
questions.explain: The standard lifecycle is to develop and test in a sandbox, then deploy to production once it works, so unfinished work is not exposed to end users.

options: A reusable blueprint describing the dashboards, datasets, and data preparation an app needs
A locked dashboard that cannot be edited
A security profile for analytics users
A saved SAQL query
questions.explain: A template describes what an app contains so new apps can be created from it, helping manage asset references and org-specific identifiers.

questions.q: What is the correct order for moving assets with change sets?
options: Deploy inbound, then upload, then create outbound
Create outbound, upload to target, then validate and deploy from inbound
Upload first, then add components
Validate in the source org, then delete the sandbox
questions.explain: You create an outbound change set in the source org, add components, upload it to the target, and then validate and deploy it from the inbound change sets there.

questions.q: You add a dataset to a change set. What does Salesforce warn about its dataflows?
options: They are deleted from the source org
They are converted to recipes automatically
They only deploy to sandboxes
They are not picked up automatically, so you must add dependent dataflows manually
questions.explain: Salesforce documentation notes that adding a dataset does not automatically add the associated dataflows, so add them yourself.

questions.q: Assets in a user's private app are a problem for deployment because...
options: They are not available for change sets, so move them to a shared app first
They are encrypted with a different key
They can only be viewed on mobile
They automatically overwrite production dashboards
questions.explain: Salesforce packaging guidance notes that assets in a private app are not available for change sets.
